thread:
Sam Patel: quick follow-up from the private cp RFC — we saw a customer failover where peering flap caused control-plane requests to fall back to the global relay and connections timed out. want to align on handshake semantics for redundant peerings.
Maria Gomez: ugh, saw the alert. do we know if it was route withdrawal or BGP session flap?
Jordan Li: looked into it — BGP session between customer VPC and our peering endpoint reset during a controlplane leader election; routes were withdrawn then re-advertised. okhttp clients timed out on long-running streaming requests.
Lee Carter: important datapoint: customer had two peering attachments (primary in us-west-2, failover in us-east-1). our controlplane tried the local peer first, then global relay. but TCP retries + TLS handshake caused 8-10s stall.
Sam Patel: proposal: make peering handshake async + speculative-config: start TCP to failover peer in parallel after X ms, but keep single TLS session to avoid double auth chattiness. thoughts on complexity?
Maria Gomez: parallel TCP attempts worry me for bursting connection counts on provider side. could we instead short-circuit by probing the local controlplane health (heartbeat) and only try parallel if heartbeat misses N times?
Jordan Li: heartbeat probe is cheaper. we could expose a light-weight UDP/HTTP health ping on carrier path that doesn't require full TLS. if probe fails -> spawn speculative TCP.
Lee Carter: sounds ok. need to be explicit about route propagation: when we do speculative connect, we must ensure we don't accidentally accept asymmetric routing (customer sees us-east IP for a connection that started with us-west). that breaks source-ip expectations if they do IP-based allowlists.
Sam Patel: good call. mitigation: attach short-lived NAT mapping tag and include origin-peering-id in TLS SNI or ALPN metadata so customer ingress can correlate and accept connections from failover peer. also document for security teams.
Maria Gomez: what about controlplane identity? if we flip peers mid-stream we need session-bound identity continuity for audit logs. can we surface a stable controlplane-session-id that transitions across peers?
Jordan Li: yes — introduce a session-id carried in a custom TLS extension or an HTTP header on the initial connect, and have both peers accept and continue the session if both trust the same KMS-signed token.
Lee Carter: ops note: we must update firewall rules doc to mention ephemeral egress IPs during speculative failover and recommended CIDR ranges. also consider quota impact on Dedicated customers.
Sam Patel: agree. action items:
- Jordan: prototype heartbeat + speculative connect (spike) and measure connection fanout (Jira #INF-2137).
- Maria: draft doc for customer security checklist and firewall guidance; call out ALPN/SNI pattern.
- Lee: estimate cost/quota surface for Dedicated and add to rollout checklist.
net-bot: deploy-check: "peering-handshake-spike" pipeline kicked off for staging at 2026-03-21T15:40Z :rocket:
Sam Patel: thanks — let's sync tomorrow at 10am PT, will bring measured numbers from the spike. :thumbsup:
